articles.author: Deena Prichep
articles.description: Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year, begins at sunset Friday. For many Jews around the world, a highlight of the holiday will be hearing the shofar: an animal's horn blown like a trumpet.
articles.title: How shofars became the spiritual soundtrack of Rosh Hashanah

articles.author: Hadeel Al-Shalchi
articles.description: Many Iranians lost their jobs because of the war and the U.S. blockade. Now some are even losing their backup jobs as sanctions tighten.
articles.title: Amid war and sanctions, many Iranians are losing their jobs and struggling to get by

articles.author: NPR Staff
articles.description: Around the U.S., ceremonies commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11th terror attacks in New York and at the Pentagon.
articles.title: In photos: Remembering the Sept. 11 attacks, 25 years later

articles.author: Rob Stein
articles.description: The worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades is growing and flu season is imminent. Experts are fretting about federal health data reliability after the CDC questioned two Pennsylvania measles deaths.
articles.title: As diseases loom, CDC's response to measles deaths stirs fears about agency's reliability

articles.author: Aisha Harris
articles.description: A Social Network follow-up, the real-life origin story of the movie Rocky, and more movies our critics are looking forward to this fall.
articles.title: 24 new movies worth checking out this fall

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Diesel prices in the U.S. has hit yet another record, soaring past $6 a gallon on average as Washington's war with Iran disrupts the world's flow of fuel
articles.title: US diesel prices soar past $6 a gallon, deepening strain for hauling everyday goods

articles.author: Holly J. Morris
articles.description: Plus: donkeys, maps, art, iPhones and more!
articles.title: Will you get $5,000 to do the news quiz? No. But will it be fun? Maybe

articles.author: Jasmine Garsd
articles.description: After 9/11, thousands of rescue and cleanup crews went to work at ground zero. They were exposed to toxic debris and experienced psychological trauma. Today, many say they live in fear of deportation.
articles.title: They cleaned up ground zero. Now many are hiding from ICE

articles.author: Stephen Fowler
articles.description: The two day Republican convention in Dallas showcased the party's biggest asset in trying to win competitive midterm races and its greatest obstacle: President Trump.
articles.title: Empty seats, socialism and Trump dominate the Republican midterm convention

articles.author: Ashley Lopez
articles.description: President Trump's tariff standoff with Canada is rankling some key voters ahead of this year's midterm elections.
articles.title: These Michigan swing voters are bracing for higher prices from trade war with Canada

articles.author: Oliver Holmes
articles.description:
Global struggle for control of Bab al-Mandab strait threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever war

Violence erupts in Yemen again: why it matters globally and how it is linked to the US-Iran war

Nearly 50,000 people have fled a sudden advance by Houthi forces in western Yemen, with entire villages emptied and families trapped near frontline fighting with depleting food supplies, according to aid workers.
Civilians in the Middle East’s poorest country have found themselves victims of a global struggle for control over one of the most important shipping routes in the world, which threatens to turn Yemen’s on-off conflict into a forever war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nearly 50,000 Yemeni civilians flee as Houthis advance along Red Sea coast

articles.author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
articles.description:
Many fear chancellor is wrong man for the job at a time when Germany’s defences against far right are crumbling
A cataclysm. A 9.0 earthquake. A five-alarm fire. A bitter rejection of Germany’s joyous reunification three decades ago, and a threat to the democratic postwar order.
Sizing up the repercussions of last weekend’s win for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party in the former communist state of Saxony-Anhalt, German commentators expressed a sense of doom, panic and helplessness in the political establishment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Firewall compromised: has Friedrich Merz blown ‘democracy’s last shot’?

articles.author: Lisa Cox
articles.description:
Former SBS newsreader had been accused by Zionist Federation of Australia of breaching Racial Discrimination Act when sharing X posts

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Federal court proceedings brought by the Zionist Federation of Australia (ZFA) against journalist Mary Kostakidis have been discontinued “by consent” with “no order as to costs”.
The former SBS newsreader had been accused by the federation of breaching the Racial Discrimination Act (RDA) by sharing two X posts about a speech by the late Hezbollah secretary general Hassan Nasrallah in January 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Court case brought by Zionist federation against journalist Mary Kostakidis ended ‘by consent’

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Prosecutors accused musician, born Durk Banks, of putting bounty on fellow rapper in retaliation for friend’s killing
Chicago rapper Lil Durk has been acquitted of all charges in a murder-for-hire scheme, in which a man was fatally gunned down in 2022.
Prosecutors had accused Lil Durk, born Durk Banks, of putting a bounty on Atlanta rapper Tayquian Bowman’s life in retaliation for the 2020 shooting death of Banks’s friend, fellow Chicago rap star King Von.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US rapper Lil Durk found not guilty of murder-for-hire scheme

articles.author: Nick Robins-Early, Lucy Campbell, Shrai Popat and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for US Breaking News emails

On 11 September, 25 years ago, Osama bin Laden drove with a small number of al-Qaida retainers and aides to a remote location in eastern Afghanistan. His convoy of SUVs was accompanied by a minivan converted into a makeshift communications centre.
The van’s rudimentary equipment did not allow Bin Laden to watch the 19 men he had started sending to the US more than a year before fly planes into the twin towers in New York and the Pentagon near Washington DC, killing about 3,000 people. But he listened as shocked radio announcers broke the news.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump keeps touting $5,000 payments if Republicans retain control of Congress as some in his party question feasibility – as it happened

articles.author: Henry Belot
articles.description:
Officers found one 14-year-old’s ebike was capable of hitting 90km/h. Owners have two weeks to appeal the seizure before the bikes will be crushed

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Dozens of high-powered and illegal ebikes have been seized by police on Sydney’s northern beaches just weeks after the force was granted new powers to destroy dangerous bikes.
The operation was part of a coordinated push with the New South Wales government to ensure people only ride legal ebikes that have not been modified to reach high speeds.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NSW police seize 36 illegal ebikes on northern beaches that are now destined for the crusher

articles.author: Guardian staff and agency
articles.description:
Two months before hacking Hugging Face, malicious packages authored by internal OpenAI agents were uploaded to RubyGems
Agents being tested by OpenAI uploaded hundreds of malicious packages in a cyberattack on software service RubyGems in May, two ⁠months ​before they hacked open-source platform Hugging Face, the company confirmed Friday.
It’s the latest revelation of cyberattacks linked to major artificial intelligence developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic. The hacks or attempts to access external systems have spooked the public and heightened concerns over the increasing abilities of AI models – and whether developers can contain them.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI agents being tested by OpenAI involved in cyber-attack on another service, say researchers

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
SF Gate reports bond for Vicky Kyung Mi Kim, 65, set at $10m after man found dead at couple’s Palm Desert home
A 65-year-old California woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder after allegedly fatally wounding her husband with a flagpole, according to SF Gate.
On 4 September, Palm Desert sheriff’s deputies responded to an “unknown trouble call” in The Enclave, a luxury condominium community. Upon arrival, officers located an individual with “traumatic injuries” that appeared to be from a physical assault and pronounced them dead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: California woman charged with murder after allegedly killing husband with flagpole

articles.author: Roque Planas and agencies
articles.description:
Police have arrested Jacques Ratliff and ruled the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black woman, as a homocide
Police in Jackson, Mississippi, have arrested a man in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black woman found hanging from a tree behind a vacant house last month. The state medical examiner on Thursday ruled Fortune’s death a homicide.
Jackson police chief RaShall Brackney-Wheelock said at a news conference Friday that police had secured search and arrest warrants for Jacques Ratliff and arrested him when they encountered him walking on the street.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man arrested over death of Mississippi woman found hanging from a tree

articles.author: Ben Doherty
articles.description:
Australia is being exploited by an ally that could draw it, however unwillingly, into war with China, experts warn

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

“Physical security matters,” said Kevin Rudd, at his axiomatic best before the National Press Club this week.
“Our first responsibility is to secure our people’s future in this most contested region of the world.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: As China rises, Australia is increasingly enmeshed in the US war machine. Is the alliance still worth the risk?

articles.author: Raphael Boyd
articles.description:
Meltdown that grounded thousands of flights caused by ‘spurious’ flight data being entered into system, report says
The air traffic control outage that caused thousands of flights to be grounded across the UK earlier in the week was caused by a military aircraft entering “spurious” flight data into the system, according to a report.
Hundreds of thousands of passengers were affected after more than 2,000 flights were cancelled on Tuesday when the system used by the National Air Traffic Services (Nats) shut down for four hours.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Military aircraft reportedly blamed for UK air traffic control outage

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The presidential briefing documents were declassified on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks
Several dozen presidential briefing documents declassified on Friday, the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, detail intelligence that government officials had gathered about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida leading up to the hijackings that killed nearly 3,000 people and upended American national security.
The documents illustrate security analysts’ tracking of Bin Laden’s movements and support system, as well as concerns about possible threats to US targets. They also detail officials’ understanding of his network in the United States and other countries, including how his operations were financed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CIA releases dozens of presidential daily briefs on Bin Laden and al-Qaida from before 9/11

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Ben Delo was convicted in US for failing to implement adequate anti-money laundering controls but pardoned by Trump
Reform UK has been given a record £36m donation by Ben Delo, a British cryptocurrency billionaire convicted in the US for failing to implement adequate anti-money laundering controls.
The businessman, who has moved back to the UK from Hong Kong, is now the biggest UK political donor by far, dwarfing the £15m contribution to Reform UK from Thailand-based Christopher Harborne.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK given record £36m donation by British crypto billionaire

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
UK employment tribunal examines whether Rockstar Games unlawfully fired 31 staff for trade union activity
A worker fired by the makers of Grand Theft Auto has said he believed employees were put on a “watch list” after signing a petition about remote working.
Dayne Oram told an employment tribunal in Glasgow examining whether Rockstar Games unlawfully fired 31 employees for trade union activity on Friday that he thought the company started keeping an eye on a group of workers after the petition was sent to leadership in 2023.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man sacked by Grand Theft Auto maker believes employees were put on ‘watch list’

articles.author: Shrai Popat and Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
President and defense secretary try to link worst terrorist attack in US history to current unpopular war

US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth used remarks at the memorial ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11 to defend the US-Israel war on Iran – and suggest the controversial conflict was part of the legacy of the worst terrorist attack in US history.
While such ceremonies on September 11 typically focus on the victims of the 2001 attacks, the US president and his defense secretary each pointed to the war they launched on Iran more than six months ago, with no end in sight.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump and Hegseth use 9/11 memorial remarks at Pentagon to defend war on Iran

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
DUP education minister accused of dragging feet before revising guidelines on uniform
Schools in Northern Ireland must give girls the choice to wear trousers as part of their uniforms as well as for PE and games, according to revised guidelines.
From next year schools would no longer be able to prohibit female pupils from wearing trousers, Paul Givan, the country’s education minister, said on Friday. “Today, I am taking that decision, that will be formally communicated, schools will be hearing from me,” he told the BBC.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Northern Ireland schools must give girls option to wear trousers from next year

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
MPs quietly withdrew support when it became clear it was not a priority of Andy Burnham’s government 

MPs vote against legalising assisted dying in England and Wales

After two years of impassioned arguments, tearful personal testimonies, noisy protests and ethical dilemmas, the assisted dying bill for England and Wales failed on a knife edge.
Campaigners on the pro side largely blame the House of Lords for making it seem an impossible struggle to get the bill through parliament, after blocking it the first time by putting through more than 1,000 amendments so that it ran out of time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why did the assisted dying bill fail in the Commons? | Rowena Mason

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll in Stockholm
articles.description:
Sweden has ordered more Britons, including vulnerable people, to leave post-Brexit than any other EU country
He arrived with nothing other than the clothes he wore that morning. Hours later he was banged up in a detention centre close to a Stockholm airport to await deportation.
Charles, a former business director from Cambridge, who did not want his full name published, moved to Sweden in 2017 to be with his Swedish wife, Lily, and applied to remain after Brexit, before the deadline of December 2021.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Absurd, hardline calls’: questions over Sweden’s post-Brexit migration policy

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
Many are rooting for vocal critic Catherine Connolly to let rip in Dublin meeting, but others hope she holds back
Catherine Connolly, Ireland’s president, once said she abhorred Donald Trump’s policies. In his sole previous comment on Connolly, the US president seemed to think she was a man. Now that they are about to meet, Ireland is holding its breath.
Trump is to fly into Dublin on Saturday morning for a two-day visit centred on golf. But before making it to his beloved greens, protocol obliges him to meet a woman who has given every impression of loathing him.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ireland holds its breath as its leftwing president prepares to meet Trump

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Rampant Yemeni fighters take control of island in narrow point of Bab al-Mandab strait, which Saudi is relying on for oil exports

Why the rapid Houthi advance matters and what’s at stake

Yemen’s rampant Houthi forces have captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait, expanding their control of the narrow waterway, one of the ​world’s vital shipping routes.
The Iran-aligned Houthis took control of the volcanic island after forces allied to the UN-backed, Aden-based government left in the latest of a dramatic series of reverses along Yemen’s west coast in recent days, including the loss of the port city of Mocha on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran’s Houthi allies capture strategic island on vital oil shipping route

articles.author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
articles.description:
Far-right German party’s newly elected representatives face fresh scrutiny as it tries to form government in Saxony-Anhalt
• Why is the AfD’s state victory significant and what might happen next?
The Alternative für Deutschland is facing scrutiny over the suitability of some of its prospective new MPs – including a former Stasi officer and a former pornography actor – just days after its historic win in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt.
Presented by the AfD’s lead candidate, Ulrich Siegmund, for a photocall in the state capital of Magdeburg on Thursday, some of the members-elect were revealed to have a range of questionable backgrounds, including criminal records, Stasi pasts and connections to far-right networks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AfD’s new state MPs include ex-Stasi officer, former porn actor, neopagans and neo-Nazis

articles.author: Jakub Krupa (now and earlier) and Martin Belam (earlier)
articles.description:
Ulf Kristersson’s comments come ahead of the parliamentary election taking place this Sunday
in Brussels
The European Commission has said it is assessing whether Ukraine has a funding shortfall, amid renewed pressure to use Russia’s frozen assets to aid Kyiv.
“That [frozen assets] is not a primary focus. We have worked extensively on this and now the focus is somewhere else.”
“So we’ve got to carry out that work first. We need to establish the needs before we can potentially discuss ways of addressing it.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sweden’s PM channels Trump saying he wants to ‘make Sweden great again’ ahead of election – as it happened

articles.author: Agence France-Press in Bangkok
articles.description:
Phra Wachirayan Wi arrested alongside woman he was filmed having sex with in latest scandal to hit country’s clergy
Police in Thailand have arrested a senior Buddhist monk on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m intended for his monastery, alongside a suspected female accomplice he was filmed having sex with.
The case is the latest scandal to hit the clergy in the Buddhist-majority country, after a sex and extortion case involving senior monks last year prompted public outrage and calls for greater scrutiny of temple finances.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Buddhist monk arrested in Thailand on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m

articles.author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: FoI documents show senior health officials were warned of concerns about assessment tool weeks after it launched

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

People with dementia were warned not to apply for home support because of fears their care would be downgraded by the government’s aged care algorithm.
Documents released to Guardian Australia under freedom of information (FoI) laws reveal the warnings came within weeks of the November rollout of the algorithm, which is used to determine funding packages and priority of need for older Australians requiring home support.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Dementia patients warned off seeking home care in case Australia’s aged care algorithm cuts funding

articles.author: Lisa Cox Environment and climate correspondent
articles.description:
Federal environment department tells industry representatives the government does not want to ‘exacerbate cost of living pressures’

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Albanese government has been accused of breaking a promise after it shelved a longstanding commitment to bring in packaging standards intended to force manufacturers and retailers to cut plastic waste.
The federal environment department told industry representatives via email last week that the promise would not be kept before the next election because the government did not want to “exacerbate cost of living pressures”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labor ditches new packaging laws to cut plastic waste, sparking unprecedented ‘scale and breadth of outrage’

articles.author: Karen McVeigh
articles.description:
Her Horizon Fund seeks $100m to stop practice harming 230m women and girls globally  
Frontline activists and leaders in the fight against female genital mutilation, which has affected more than 230 million women and girls worldwide, have welcomed an unprecedented $15.5m (£11.4m) fund aimed at creating “unstoppable momentum” to finally end the practice.
The launch of the fund comes as women’s rights are increasingly under attack and donor funding is in sharp decline, particularly for work led by FGM survivors in local communities. It is thought to be the largest single philanthropic contribution to ending the practice of FGM.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: $15m fund launched to create ‘unstoppable momentum’ to end FGM worldwide

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Canadian PM Mark Carney hosts president in Calgary, where he grew up alongside large Ukrainian community
Canada offered support on Thursday to boost Ukraine’s air defenses and help replenish its drone stocks, as the countries pledged to deepen their alliance during a visit by Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Mark Carney hosted the president of Ukraine in Calgary in the western province of Alberta, where the Canadian prime minister grew up among a large community of people with Ukrainian heritage.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada offers air defense support for Ukraine as Zelenskyy visits

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Family of late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV reject committee’s choice of cousin and TV presenter as new monarch
A traditional Ugandan kingdom has become engulfed in a bitter succession dispute after the family of a king who recently died rejected the selection of a television news anchor as his successor.
King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the throne in the kingdom of Tooro in 1995 at the age of three, died on 27 August in the US, where he was receiving cancer treatment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Secret son revelation ignites bitter succession dispute in Ugandan kingdom

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem and Xan Brooks in Venice
articles.description:
Testimony from Israeli military insiders involved in surveillance and remote killings features in documentary produced by the Guardian

Testimony from 24 Israeli military insiders ​on the secret ​systems used in ​the war on Gaza​ has been revealed in a new documentary film about the mass killing of Palestinian civilians.
NAZA, a film from the Oscar-winning Israeli directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, was shown at the Venice international film festival on Thursday as the only documentary competing for its prestigious Golden Lion award.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Secret systems used by Israel in mass killings of Gaza civilians revealed in new film

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Tokyo
articles.description:
The new ‘true-scale’ map shrinks Europe and North America while enlarging Africa – and depicts the disputed Kuril islands as ruled by Moscow
Japan has asked for the revision of a new world map adopted by the UN because it said it made the disputed Kuril islands appear to belong to Russia.
The UN general assembly voted on Friday to adopt the new map, which makes the African continent larger while also shrinking North America and Europe, drawing condemnation from the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan seeks change to new UN world map over Russia 'misconception'

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Iran and its proxies move closer to full control of two shipping chokepoints as regional conflict widens

Explained: why the fighting in Yemen matters globally

Houthi forces in Yemen are making a concerted drive to take over the country’s Red Sea coast fully, claiming control of the key port of Mocha in the most serious wave of fighting with the Saudi-backed government in years, bringing the Iran-aligned group closer to full control of a key shipping route.
Seizure of the coast and some of the islands in the sea would be a strategic disaster for Saudi Arabia and the US, taking Iran and its proxies closer to full control of two choke points for western shipping on opposite sides of the Arabian peninsula: the Bab al-Mandab at the southern end of the Red Sea and the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houthis seize key Yemeni port of Mocha in drive to take control of Red Sea coast

articles.author: Tora Agarwala
articles.description:
Following six years of talks, Pitt Rivers Museum will return body parts collected by British colonial administrators to north-east India
Anthropologists and community leaders from Nagaland, a remote state in north-eastern India bordering Myanmar, have expressed joy and relief that human remains belonging to their ancestors that had been on display in a British museum for nearly a century are finally being returned.
On Monday, the Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford announced that 39 pieces of human remains – including parts of skulls, a finger and a piece of skin with hair – belonging to the Naga tribes, will be returned to Nagaland after six years of negotiation between the community and the museum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Our forefathers are coming back’: Naga people celebrate after Oxford museum agrees to return remains

articles.author: Danny Vincent in Hong Kong
articles.description:
Dow Jones convicted of one count of deterring Selina Cheng from role at Hong Kong Journalist Association but cleared of second charge
A Hong Kong court has convicted the publisher of the Wall Street Journal of deterring a reporter from taking up a trade union role, in a case that raised concerns about press freedom in the city.
The newspaper dismissed Selina Cheng just weeks after she was appointed chair of the Hong Kong Journalist Association (HKJA) in 2024. She was told at the time her termination was officially due to restructuring.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wall Street Journal publisher convicted in Hong Kong of deterring reporter from union role

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Multiple search and rescue vessels deployed after blaze off Palawan island leaves at least five dead, says coast guard
A large-scale ⁠search and rescue operation ​is under way off the western Philippine island of Palawan on Thursday after a passenger ferry caught fire, killing five people and leaving ⁠scores of passengers missing.
The Philippine coast guard said multiple vessels and other assets were searching for survivors as rescue teams used drift-modelling tools ⁠to identify areas where people may have been carried by currents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Deadly Philippines ferry fire triggers search for scores of missing

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
The International Atomic Energy Agency voices ‘serious concerns’ over expansion of Yongbyon facility to enrich uranium
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has voiced “serious concern” over evidence that North Korea has built a facility capable of enriching weapons-grade uranium to bolster its nuclear arsenal.
The new building, located at the the country’s main Yongbyon nuclear facility, can house up to 28 centrifuge cascades – machinery commonly used to enrich uranium – according to a report by the nuclear watchdog released this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: North Korea has built new uranium facility to expand nuclear arsenal, UN agency says

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Rubio visits Ecuador and welcomes cooperation after campaign of unilateral strikes on alleged ‘narco-terrorists’
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, gave new clarity on the approach toward combating drug trafficking in Latin American waters, saying the Trump administration was focused on working with allied countries and aligning with their laws but insisted the military would “still blow up ships if need be”.
The public acknowledgment of a shift in US strategy comes a year after Washington began a campaign of unilateral deadly strikes against those it calls “narco-terrorists” operating boats in international waters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rubio signals shift to working with allies to fight drug trade as latest boat strike kills three

articles.author: Andrew Roth and agencies
articles.description:
Trump administration to seek extra funding from Congress to ‘dismantle’ Los Tiguerones over narcotics trafficking
The US has designated Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones gang, which stormed a television station during a live broadcast in 2024, as a terrorist organisation as the Trump administration expands its campaign against narcotics traffickers it says are destabilising Latin America.
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, made the announcement in Quito, where he met Ecuadorian president Daniel Noboa, one of several rightwing allies of Donald Trump whom Rubio is courting as a security partner during a three-nation tour through Latin America that began on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Notorious Ecuadorian crime gang designated a terrorist group by US

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba announces decision to pull out in post on X, citing tensions over ‘Harry-Meghan nonsense’
Uganda is withdrawing from the Duke of Sussex’s Invictus Games, the country’s military chief has said, out of respect for King Charles amid division over the “Harry-Meghan nonsense”.
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of the Ugandan president, made the surprise announcement in a post on X on Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Uganda to withdraw from Invictus Games ‘out of respect for King Charles’, says military chief

articles.author: Natricia Duncan and agencies
articles.description:
Andrew Frederick’s body was found in property he was staying at in Grenada in January
The family of a British father who was found dead in the Caribbean in January is urging authorities in Grenada to work with UK police to uncover the truth about his death.
Andrew Frederick’s body was found in the property he was staying at in Grenada on 4 January. An autopsy, performed in the same week by a privately hired pathologist, concluded that the 47-year-old’s death was a homicide.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Family of British man found dead in Grenada ask local police to work with UK investigators

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Three men are on trial over the death of brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend, US citizen Jack Carter Rhoad, in Ensenada
The father of two Australian surfers killed in Mexico two years ago testified in court on Tuesday that his life had been turned into hell, as the high-profile trial continued into its second day.
Three men are charged in the killing of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, respectively, and their 30-year-old American friend Jack Carter Rhoad, who were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast in April 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s hell’: father of slain Australian surfers tells Mexico homicide trial about identifying sons’ bodies

articles.author: Kat Lay, Global health correspondent
articles.description:
Key regions of the brain linked to movement, learning and emotions were affected and may lead to cognitive problems 
Babies born to mothers with anaemia have smaller brains, particularly in key regions linked to movement, learning and the regulation of emotion, according to a study.
Researchers said the differences, first detected at the age of one, could lead to cognitive problems when children started school.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Babies born to anaemic mothers have smaller brains, study finds

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have eroded
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.
Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Trust deficit’: Why India’s economic data has sparked a furore

articles.author: Mohamed Gabobe in Mogadishu and Peter Beaumont
articles.description:
US-Israel war on Iran and political instability in Somalia lead to pirates targeting cargo ships off Horn of Africa
The scourge of Somali piracy targeting cargo ships and smaller dhows off the Horn of Africa has returned to levels not seen in a decade, driven by a convergence of factors including disruptions to the shipping industry caused by the US-Israeli war against Iran and a resurgence of political instability in Somalia.
Since late April there have been eight hijackings by Somali pirates, including two within the space of a fortnight in August: one targeting an oil tanker with ties to Iran, the other a Cameroon-flagged vessel, the Lutuf, carrying military equipment for Turkey.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hijacking pirates exploit regional chaos to return to seas off Somalia

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Kathmandu
articles.description:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions 
Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.
Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation
Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal.
The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Washington Post report also reveals Jon Husted staffer Stephen Woytek created pro-Rhodesia playlist on Spotify 
The Republican senator for Ohio, Jon Husted, has fired an aide who was discovered to have used a photo of Nazi SS soldiers as his Facebook profile photo.
Stephen Woytek was appointed as Husted’s political director last month in the senator’s knife-edge re-election contest against former Democrat senator Sherrod Brown. According to the Washington Post, Husted had decided to “part ways” with Woytek, 25, after learning that his Facebook profile showed he followed a military re-enactment group called LAH Living History Unit, which portrays the 1st SS Panzer division.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican senator fires aide who used Nazi soldiers as Facebook profile picture

articles.author: Aram Roston and agencies
articles.description:
Joe diGenova led investigation focused on intelligence assessment that Russia interfered in 2016 election
A longtime ally of Donald Trump resigned from his post leading a Department of Justice investigation into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired against the Republican president.
“Sometimes people want things done faster and that’s all you can do,” Joe diGenova told the Guardian on Thursday. He appeared to be referring to concerns among other Trump loyalists that the president’s retribution cases were not moving quickly enough.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump ally resigns from post leading inquiry into alleged conspiracy against president

articles.author: Tom Perkins
articles.description:
Mike Rogers has also helped kill other bills that would have provided healthcare to responders and survivors
Mike Rogers, a Michigan Republican US Senate candidate, has sought in recent weeks to create controversy over old tweets his Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed posted about 9/11. He has for example, falsely suggested El-Sayed, who is Muslim, said the US deserved the attack.
But, as critics have noted, Rogers has twice voted against healthcare and other benefits for 9/11 first responders and survivors, congressional records show. He has also helped kill other bills that would have provided benefits and healthcare to first responders nationwide. Rogers, a former member of Congress, is vying for Michigan’s open US Senate seat in a tight race that could decide control of Congress during the next session.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican seeking to implicate Abdul El-Sayed over 9/11 voted twice against benefits for first responders

articles.author: Shrai Popat and Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
President and defense secretary try to link worst terrorist attack in US history to current unpopular war

US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth used remarks at the memorial ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11 to defend the US-Israel war on Iran – and suggest the controversial conflict was part of the legacy of the worst terrorist attack in US history.
While such ceremonies on September 11 typically focus on the victims of the 2001 attacks, the US president and his defense secretary each pointed to the war they launched on Iran more than six months ago, with no end in sight.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump and Hegseth use 9/11 memorial remarks at Pentagon to defend war on Iran

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Café Niederegger | Reading’s Bayeux tapestry | Trump’s renaming spree | The  Amerigo Round
In her piece on Lübeck (‘Fabulous museums and no queues’: five of the best under-the-radar city breaks in Europe, 6 September), Rachel Dixon didn’t mention the German city’s sweetest treat, the Café Niederegger. Many will know the city’s name from Niederegger marzipan as much as Thomas Mann. Their museum on the floor above the cafe includes a lifesize marzipan statue of the writer, whom they claim was also a fan.
Elizabeth Card
Leeds
• It is surprising that Reading Museum has not used the publicity surrounding the arrival of the Bayeux tapestry in the UK to blow its own trumpet more loudly. Its superb copy of the Bayeux tapestry, produced by 35 women in just over a year, finishing in 1886, is free to view.
Joyce Quarrie
Leytonstone, London
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lübeck’s sweetest treat deserves a visit | Brief letters

articles.author: Jameel Jaffer
articles.description:
Over the past quarter-century, the US supreme court has repeatedly failed to protect first amendment rights. We are suffering the consequences
Congress ratified the first amendment in 1791 but the supreme court didn’t breathe life into it until after the first world war, when prosecutions of antiwar protesters led the justices Oliver Wendell Holmes and Louis Brandeis – and then, fortunately, other justices as well – to realize that US democracy would be undermined, not strengthened, by allowing the government to suppress disfavored political opinions.
Repression during the cold war led the court to better protect the freedom of association, and government efforts to cover up official ineptitude and criminality during the Vietnam war spurred the court to better protect the freedom of the press. It took time, but in each of these instances the court responded to wartime repression by developing new legal doctrine that more robustly protected first amendment freedoms.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The ‘war on terror’ weakened the first amendment. Now we desperately need it | Jameel Jaffer

articles.author: Simon Jenkins
articles.description:
The US president is ever more wayward – and has little interest in defending Europe. The constitution may hold him to account, but we can’t wait
If Americans vote for a Republican majority in both houses of Congress in November, “I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000.” But they must not spend it in Canada or China or anywhere else outside the US. So said Donald Trump in Texas on Wednesday in advance of the forthcoming midterm elections. He further told voters to “Pretend that I’m on the ballot”. It was a climactic moment in an almost two-hour rant.
Trump does not have the required trillion dollars in his pocket, and it would be illegal to disperse such a sum without congressional approval. In any case, JD Vance now appears to have rowed back on the promise.
Simon Jenkins is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wake up, Britain: Donald Trump’s US is no friend of ours. We must secure our own place in the world  | Simon Jenkins

articles.author: Presented by Jenna Amatulli , with Rachel Leingang , produced by Nada Smiljanic and John Rogers. The executive producer was Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Donald Trump has thrown a convention to amp up the Republican base ahead of the midterm elections, but not everyone is thrilled about it. Dozens of officials running for re-election have stayed away, choosing instead to campaign locally. Are they worried about Trump’s current unpopularity weighing down their ticket?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump-a-palooza: why are Republicans avoiding the president? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
The White House posted a photo of bald eagle attacking a Canada goose to send a message – but it was Canada that played a critical role in the recovery of the bird in the US
In late August, the White House posted a real photograph on social media of a bald eagle standing atop the limp neck of a Canada goose.
The raptor presses the goose’s face into the grey winter slush. With its stark white head and brilliant yellow talons, the eagle looks victorious and defiant.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada helped save the bald eagle from near extinction in the US – does the White House know?

articles.author: danah boyd
articles.description:
The very mechanisms that allow the census bureau to resist partisan interference are coming undone. And Congress is silent
When the constitutional architects of the United States got together, they came up with a crazy plan: “What if we count everyone in the country and allocate political representation that way?”
It was a radical act. Until then, censuses had been used by kings to levy taxes and conscript men into war. With the penning of article 1, section 2 of the US constitution, being counted ensured that states would get financial resources and political representatives. Congress was tasked with building the processes to anchor representation to the population. People wanted to be counted. And politicians wanted their people to be counted more.
danah boyd is the Geri Gay professor of communication at Cornell University and the author of Data Are Made, Not Found: A Story of Politics, Power, and the Civil Servants Who Saved the US Census
 Continue reading...
articles.title: American democracy depends on the census. Trump is undermining it | danah boyd

articles.author: Ted Widmer
articles.description:
President suggested US might not help UK if Argentina tried to seize Falklands – a new low for UK-US ‘special relationship’
Last week, Donald Trump suggested in an interview with the British TV channel GB News that he might not help the UK if Argentina tried again to seize the Falkland Islands. It was a new low for UK-US relations.
The “special relationship” (Winston Churchill’s phrase) was never perfect, but the UK helped the US on countless occasions, from Korea to Iraq to Afghanistan. The US often stood by the UK as well – although not during the Suez Crisis of 1956, but Ronald Reagan’s government provided significant intelligence and logistics support to Britain during the dust-up over the Falklands in 1982. That relationship is fading fast.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s comments on the Falkland Islands reflect a fractured US-UK relationship

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright with J Oliver Conroy , produced by Tiara Chiaramonte , engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Jonathan Menjivar
articles.description:
Charlie Kirk's death created a vacuum of power that still consumes the Maga right a year later. Immediately after Kirk was shot and killed, his ultraconservative activist organization Turning Point USA announced that his widow, Erika Kirk, would replace her late husband as CEO. But as Guardian reporter J Oliver Conroy tells Kai Wright, conspiracy theories pushed by Kirk's former allies and proteges have dogged both the organization and Erika Kirk herself. Real questions remain about whether Erika Kirk can maintain the enormous power and influence Turning Point holds on the right and what she is planning to do with the organization. Conroy spent months reporting on Charlie Kirk’s legacy talking to dozens of people within Turning Point USA and the larger Maga movement who view Charlie Kirk as a martyr. Conroy says martyrdom is a powerful force that can’t be controlled


J Oliver Conroy's Guardian story on Charlie Kirk and Turning Point USA:  Grief, fury, conspiracy: inside Turning Point USA after Charlie Kirk’s killing

 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Charlie Kirk's martyrdom fed the right. And then tore it apart – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.description:
Donald Trump pledged to pay every adult citizen in the US a $5,000 dividend if the Republicans retain the House and Senate in the midterms, during a rambling speech at the party's midterm convention in Dallas.
The US president claimed the payment was possible due to the country's 'tremendous economic success, like in history we've never had anything like what's happening'. The  proposal, which would cost more than $1tn, immediately raised ethical concerns


US citizens will receive $5,000 if Republicans win midterms, Trump claims


 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump: we will pay every US citizen $5,000 if Republicans win midterms – video

articles.author: David Smith in Dallas
articles.description:
President’s quest in self-mythology stops off in Dallas for a Republican convention where fans indulged his lies and revelled in his jokes
Kim Il-sung of North Korea reportedly sought transfusions of blood from young men; Mao Zedong of China believed sex with young women could prolong his life; Muammar Gaddafi underwent fat injections and hair transplantation to make himself look younger. But for Donald Trump, the secret of eternal youth lies in nights like this.
The occasion of the Republican midterm convention in Dallas was enough to get the 80-year-old US president’s juices flowing. An arena with thousands of fanatical supporters indulging his lies, laughing at his jokes and burnishing his fantasies of greatness is Trump’s happy place.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: As the midterms loom, Trump returns to his happy place: on stage in the theatre of the absurd

articles.author: Jason Burke International security correspondent
articles.description:
Budget cuts, loss of knowledgeable officials and diverted resources raise risk of another attack, experts warn
The US faces growing challenges in countering international terrorism as resources are diverted to other threats, experienced security officials leave and “complacency” spreads, experts have warned.
It is 25 years this week since the 9/11 attacks launched by Osama bin Laden’s al-Qaida on New York and Washington, which killed about 3,000 people and led to decades of conflict, radicalisation and instability across the Middle East and beyond.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Institutional neglect’: 25 years on from 9/11, experts sound alarm over US counter-terror efforts

articles.author: Adam Gabbatt in Dallas, Texas
articles.description:
GOP plans to center the president at rare two-day Texas event as party hopes to retain control of House in midterms
Republicans are gathering in Texas on Wednesday for a rare “midterm convention”, as they attempt to convince Americans to vote for a party led by a deeply unpopular president who has overseen inflation and led the US into an increasingly unpopular war.
Donald Trump will dominate the two-day convention, appearing both nights as the GOP works to cling to control of the House of Representatives in November. Republicans plan to put the president at the center of the event, a bold strategy given his approval rating is hovering at about 38%, while accusing the Democratic party of being socialist and out of touch with Americans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republicans kick off ‘midterm convention’ to overcome Trump unpopularity

articles.description:
The Canadian province's premier, Doug Ford, installed a billboard-sized sign on the lake's shoreline after the US president signed an executive order on Thursday directing US federal agencies to change the lake's name on US maps, documents and databases to 'Lake America'. Ford told reporters that the lake's name, which is more than 400 years old, would remain unchanged. Trade talks between the US and Canada collapsed last week, with each side ‌blaming the ⁠other for derailing three days of intensive negotiations


Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ontario premier unveils Lake Ontario sign in response to Trump’s ‘Lake America’ order – video

articles.author: Raphael Boyd
articles.description:
Meltdown that grounded thousands of flights caused by ‘spurious’ flight data being entered into system, report says
The air traffic control outage that caused thousands of flights to be grounded across the UK earlier in the week was caused by a military aircraft entering “spurious” flight data into the system, according to a report.
Hundreds of thousands of passengers were affected after more than 2,000 flights were cancelled on Tuesday when the system used by the National Air Traffic Services (Nats) shut down for four hours.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Military aircraft reportedly blamed for UK air traffic control outage

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Ben Delo was convicted in US for failing to implement adequate anti-money laundering controls but pardoned by Trump
Reform UK has been given a record £36m donation by Ben Delo, a British cryptocurrency billionaire convicted in the US for failing to implement adequate anti-money laundering controls.
The businessman, who has moved back to the UK from Hong Kong, is now the biggest UK political donor by far, dwarfing the £15m contribution to Reform UK from Thailand-based Christopher Harborne.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK given record £36m donation by British crypto billionaire

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
UK employment tribunal examines whether Rockstar Games unlawfully fired 31 staff for trade union activity
A worker fired by the makers of Grand Theft Auto has said he believed employees were put on a “watch list” after signing a petition about remote working.
Dayne Oram told an employment tribunal in Glasgow examining whether Rockstar Games unlawfully fired 31 employees for trade union activity on Friday that he thought the company started keeping an eye on a group of workers after the petition was sent to leadership in 2023.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man sacked by Grand Theft Auto maker believes employees were put on ‘watch list’

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
DUP education minister accused of dragging feet before revising guidelines on uniform
Schools in Northern Ireland must give girls the choice to wear trousers as part of their uniforms as well as for PE and games, according to revised guidelines.
From next year schools would no longer be able to prohibit female pupils from wearing trousers, Paul Givan, the country’s education minister, said on Friday. “Today, I am taking that decision, that will be formally communicated, schools will be hearing from me,” he told the BBC.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Northern Ireland schools must give girls option to wear trousers from next year

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
MPs quietly withdrew support when it became clear it was not a priority of Andy Burnham’s government 

MPs vote against legalising assisted dying in England and Wales

After two years of impassioned arguments, tearful personal testimonies, noisy protests and ethical dilemmas, the assisted dying bill for England and Wales failed on a knife edge.
Campaigners on the pro side largely blame the House of Lords for making it seem an impossible struggle to get the bill through parliament, after blocking it the first time by putting through more than 1,000 amendments so that it ran out of time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why did the assisted dying bill fail in the Commons? | Rowena Mason

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Opponents say proposed law change for England and Wales was ‘unsafe and unworkable’ after bill is narrowly defeated
As it became clear that MPs had voted against the assisted dying bill, campaigners who had fought for a change in the law looked broken. Standing outside the Houses of Parliament, many wearing pink caps and T-shirts with slogans such as “Give me choice over my death”, they held on to each other for comfort. Some were in tears, others stood in shocked silence.
MP Lauren Edwards, who sponsored the bill that would have allowed terminally ill adults in England and Wales with six months or less to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives, said its failure to pass was disappointing “for the many thousands of terminally ill people and their loved ones who were given hope when the Commons voted for this bill last year”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A tragic day’: campaigners react as MPs say no to legalising assisted dying

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Proceeds are in a UK account amid a dispute about how the money should be used and a separate criminal investigation
Funds from Roman Abramovich’s sale of Chelsea FC have earned at least £175m in interest while locked in a UK bank account, new accounts show, leading one analyst to describe the company housing the frozen cash as “the most profitable football business in the world”.
Accounts for Fordstam, the company through which the billionaire Russian oligarch owned Chelsea, show that the proceeds of the sale completed in May 2022 have risen from £2.3bn to nearly £2.5bn.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘World’s most profitable football business’: Abramovich’s frozen Chelsea cash earns £175m

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Democrat Ron Wyden and Republican Warren Davidson tell investigatory powers tribunal that secrecy over encrypted data case is ‘needlessly’ straining US-UK relations
A bipartisan pair of American politicians is telling Britain’s most secretive court to stop hiding its handling of Apple’s legal fight against a government demand to break into its customers’ encrypted data, warning that Whitehall’s taste for secrecy is “needlessly” straining relations between the two allies.
The letter, shared with the Guardian ahead of being sent to the investigatory powers tribunal (IPT) on Friday, is signed by the Democratic senator Ron Wyden of Oregon and the Republican congressman Warren Davidson of Ohio.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US lawmakers urge secretive British court to open up about Apple case

articles.author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
articles.description:
Letter from 70 MPs and peers follows Anthropic employee’s claim new technology could wipe out humans

AI could kill all humans in next decade, warn experts: but how seriously should we take them?

More than 70 MPs and peers have urged Andy Burnham to back a ban on the creation of artificial superintelligence (ASI) and lead an international movement to stop the technology after a week of warnings from experts of a 10% chance it could kill all humans.
Fifteen former government ministers, along with the former head of the civil service Robin Butler, senior Labour MPs including John McDonnell and leading Conservatives, Liberal Democrat and Scottish National party MPs have written to the prime minister. They urged him to throw the government’s weight behind a bill, tabled in the Commons on Tuesday, that would prohibit ASI – an as-yet-nonexistent AI that would outcompete human capabilities in most domains.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK lawmakers urge Burnham to back ban on superintelligent AI after chilling warnings

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Bill’s failure in Commons sparks anger among its supporters after Lords blocked earlier legislation
A renewed attempt to legalise assisted dying has been voted down by MPs in a decision that is likely to scupper the idea for a political generation, sparking anger among supporters after an earlier bill was blocked by the Lords.
A private member’s bill put forward by Labour’s Lauren Edwards, which would have permitted assisted dying in England and Wales in certain limited circumstances, was defeated by 286 to 270 at second reading, the first chance MPs have to vote on a measure.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MPs vote against legalising assisted dying in England and Wales

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Report says widespread autonomous vehicle adoption would put hundreds of thousands of private hire jobs at risk
Taxes on self-driving cars should be introduced now in the UK to offset the rise in congestion and threats to jobs they pose, a thinktank has urged.
The first robotaxis on London’s streets only started this month, but government projections are that up to 40% of cars sold could have self-driving capability by the middle of the next decade.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Self-driving cars should be taxed to offset job losses, thinktank urges

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now) and Taz Ali (earlier)
articles.description:
The bill would have allowed terminally ill adults with less than six months to live to end their lives, after the approval of a panel of experts

MPs vote against legalising assisted dying in England and Wales

While the debate continues, we have a comment from Sam Royston, executive director of research and policy at Marie Curie. He said the government must address the crisis in palliative care regardless of what happens with assisted dying, calling for a new framework and funding to ensure everyone has access to compassionate end-of-life care.
He said:
Whatever happens with assisted dying, the UK government must fix the crisis in palliative care.
It is devastating that nearly one in three people die without the help they need. Too many spend their final days in pain or on busy, chaotic hospital wards, while families are left fighting for help instead of spending time with the people they love.
I think it’s absolutely right that, for instance, the prime minister and the government have said that improving palliative care must be a priority for him and his government. I think that’s something that we can all support.
I think everybody should have access to good quality palliative and hospice end-of-life care at their final moment.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MPs reject assisted dying bill after tense debate – as it happened

articles.author: Zoe Wood
articles.description:
Substitution with jack mackerel, a different species, because of dwindling stocks is criticised by consumer group Which?
If you’ve recently opened a tin of mackerel and thought there was something fishy going on, you may have been right. An overfishing crisis means that instead of traditional mackerel, some now contain a different fish with a similar name, prompting concerns that shoppers are being short-changed.
Over the past year big brands such as Princes, as well as some supermarket own labels, have replaced traditional tinned mackerel fillets with jack mackerel fillets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Extra fishy: your tinned mackerel may not be what you think it is

articles.author: Rowena Mason and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Greens accuse Labour of hiding position to avoid criticism before contest, in which Zack Polanski is standing
A decision on approving the controversial Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea is to be delayed until later this autumn, with the Greens accusing Labour of hiding their position before the crucial Holborn and St Pancras byelection.
Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, had been poised to give her recommendation to approve the Jackdaw field off the coast of Aberdeen next week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: North Sea gasfield decision likely delayed until after Holborn and St Pancras byelection

articles.author: Seán Clarke
articles.description:
MPs today voted not to approve the assisted dying bill at its second reading. The bill, which was brought back to the Commons after being blocked in the Lords, would have allowed terminally ill people to end their lives with medical help in some circumstances. Find out how your MP voted
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How did your MP vote on the reintroduced assisted dying bill?

articles.description:
MPs have been debating a bill to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales. The bill would allow terminally ill adults with less than six months to live to end their lives, after the approval of a panel of experts. Speaking in the Commons, Labour's Claire Hazelgrove, who is in favour of the bill, said her mother, Ruth, died alone last October after living with a rare blood cancer for half of her life. Fellow Labour MP Ashley Dalton, who has been diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer, said the assisted dying bill does not adequately protect people with treatable depression who also have a terminal illness

UK politics: latest updates

 Continue reading...
articles.title: MPs recount personal experiences as they debate assisted dying bill – video

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Party leader, who will contest Starmer’s former seat of Holborn and St Pancras, says gas drilling has come up on doorstep
Zack Polanski has said a vote for him in the upcoming Holborn and St Pancras byelection is a vote against the government’s reported plans to greenlight a North Sea gasfield.
The leader of the Green party in England and Wales, who was selected on Friday to contest the London seat, also said he was considering building a personal stockpile for the extreme weather predicted with the arrival of the biggest El Niño in 1,000 years, a meteorological phenomenon that supercharges floods and droughts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: People ‘incensed’ by North Sea plans can vote Green in byelection, says Zack Polanski

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Businesses, charities and other groups sign letter calling for levies to be paid by the government
More than 120 organisations including big businesses and charities have called for the removal of “hidden taxes” added to energy bills to help reduce costs for consumers and prevent businesses closing.
In a letter to the chancellor the signatories – including Energy UK, business trade body the CBI, End Fuel Poverty and Age UK – called for levies amounting to 10% of energy bills that fund policies to be paid for by the government. John Healey is to present his first budget on 28 October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK chancellor urged to remove ‘hidden taxes’ from energy bills

articles.author: Matthew Taylor
articles.description:
At least 760,000 children in England and Wales missed lessons as more than 1,700 schools closed or finished early
The gruelling heatwave that hit the UK in June caused pupils to miss more than 15m hours of lesson time as soaring temperatures forced hundreds of schools to close, according to a study.
The research found that at least 760,000 schoolchildren in England and Wales missed lessons owing to closures during the heatwave – one of five in the UK this summer – as temperatures inside some classrooms topped 40C (104F), leaving pupils and staff suffering from heat stress, nausea and headaches.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pupils missed 15m hours of school time during UK’s June heatwave, study finds

articles.author: Alex Daniel and Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
From Shropshire to Hamburg, depleting reserves and spiralling costs are spawning a continent-wide energy crisis
Bridgnorth Aluminium has faced down Brexit, Covid and repeated energy shocks in recent years. But this winter is bringing extra “stress and pressure”, says its head of sales, Adrian Musgrave.
Musgrave’s company makes rolled aluminium, used in packaging, construction and the manufacture of items such as cars and batteries. Like many stretched industrial businesses across Europe, Bridgnorth Aluminium faces a looming threat of soaring energy bills, which Musgrave describes as “just worry upon worry”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Just worry upon worry’: Europe faces a bleak winter as supply shock pushes factories to the brink

articles.author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
articles.description:
Welcome boost for chancellor with unexpected rise put down to rapid growth of AI in services sector outweighing Iran war fallout 
The UK economy grew in July as the rapid expansion of AI appeared to outweigh the economic damage from the Iran war, in a welcome boost for John Healey.
Figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed a surprise 0.4% increase in gross domestic product (GDP), compared with 0.3% growth in June. City economists had forecast zero growth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK economy unexpectedly grows 0.4% in July boosted by AI

articles.author: Ben Quinn and Neha Gohil
articles.description:
Nigel Farage said demonstrators in balaclavas were ‘horrible’, but others in the party defend them as ‘brave, passionate patriots’
Nigel Farage’s condemnation of the masked men whose blockade of Dover stole headlines on the final day of his party’s annual conference was swift, describing their actions as “horrible”.
Yet less than a week on from the public debut of the black-clad members of Patriot Platform, Reform is gripped with internal friction over the activists. There has been unease among some members and councillors about Farage’s criticism and some outright praise for the group as “patriots”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK beset by internal row over response to Dover and Portsmouth protests

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Heather Stewart; produced by Eleanor Biggs, Saskia Collette and Brian McNamara; executive producer Homa Khaleeli
articles.description:
The UK foreign secretary has drawn rage and respect after announcing trade sanctions on Israeli settlers. Heather Stewart explains how – and why – Ed Miliband got tough
This time just over a decade ago, Ed Miliband was known for pushing his older brother David out of the way to become leader of the Labour party … only to lose the 2015 general election and become an internet meme for eating a bacon sandwich. But through the last 10 years, Miliband seems to have undergone a quiet transformation.
This week he condemned Israel’s “settler terrorists”, saying they were ethnically cleansing the West Bank, his condemnation breaking decades-long government policy on UK-Israel relations. And, his supporters say, he’s only just getting started.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ed Stone to elder statesman: the making of Ed Miliband – podcast

articles.author: Chris Wiegand Stage editor
articles.description:
The Ali G and Borat creator is reported to be taking the lead in The Popinjay Cavalier, a swashbuckling comedy Tarantino is developing for early 2027
He will soon be seen resuming his old Staines rudeboy persona in the film 
Ali G: Who Iz I?, but Sacha Baron Cohen may also be eyeing a new departure – on stage.
The actor will reportedly star in Quentin Tarantino’s first play, The Popinjay Cavalier, which is billed as a “rambunctious comedy of deception and disguise” and a “sweeping celebration of theatre and its heightened romance”, set in 1830s Europe. According to Deadline, Baron Cohen will play the swashbuckling title character in the play, which Tarantino will also direct.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen lined up for Quentin Tarantino’s West End playwriting debut

articles.description:
Hundreds queued outside the British Museum on Thursday as the exhibit of the Bayeux tapestry opened. The 70 metre-long masterpiece will be on show in London for 10 months, having left France for the first time since the 11th century. Believed to have been sewn by English seamstresses before being taken to France, the embroidery tells the story of the events leading up to the Battle of Hastings and the subsequent Norman defeat of the Anglo-Saxon King Harold II

The Bayeux tapestry: why more women should be stitched into history

A stupefying, thrilling, horrifying masterpiece that shakes the earth

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Visitors delighted to see Bayeux tapestry on display in the UK for the first time – video

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Studies from hotspots across Europe that have introduced levies suggest they have no impact on visitor numbers
If you wandered down Las Ramblas or lazed on a beach in the Balearics this summer, you probably paid a tourist tax for the privilege. In fact, if you enjoyed any of Europe’s beauty spots in recent years, it is likely that an overnight levy was added to your bill.
Britons have become used to paying these fees abroad but ministers have shied away from introducing them in the UK. The furious response from UK hospitality bosses helps to explain why.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The hospitality industry fears a tourist tax will deter visitors – the evidence says otherwise

articles.author: Rob Davies, Elena Morresi, Karif Wat, Sarah Bertram and Boglarka Kosztolanyi
articles.description:
French company Puy du Fou is planning a £600m history-themed park in Oxfordshire. A Guardian investigation has found the company continued working with associates of Konstantin Malofeyev, a pro-Kremlin oligarch under sanctions, on plans for a theme park in Russian-occupied Crimea for longer than it had previously disclosed, and later explored projects in Iran and China.

Business reporter Rob Davies explains his findings, including documents that raise questions about whether Puy du Fou’s activities tested the limits of EU sanctions imposed after Russia’s 2014 annexation of Crimea.

He also examines the far-right politics associated with Puy du Fou’s founder, Philippe de Villiers, and asks whether the company is a suitable choice to tell Britain’s national story


Kremlin connections: the Russia links to a £600m UK theme park

 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Russia-tied French billionaires opening UK's first historical theme park – explainer

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Record demand for A&E units, ambulance services and NHS 111 shows extreme heat having unprecedented impact on health, experts say
The NHS came under its most intense strain ever as a result of the summer’s five heatwaves, amid warnings that extreme heat is having an unprecedented impact on human health.
A&E units, ambulance services and the NHS 111 telephone advice line all experienced record demand for their services in England in June, July and August as Britain experienced record temperatures.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS reports busiest ever summer as heatwaves drive up hospital admissions

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Hot weather means sweeter grapes, but outlook gloomier for beermakers, as drought diminishes barley harvest

English sparkling winemakers expect their earliest grape harvest and a “vintage year” after a scorching summer quickly ripened grapes.
However, beer sellers have warned of a potential shortage after record-breaking temperatures and a drought hitting much of England has caused poor yields of barley.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: English winemakers expect ‘vintage year’ after record-breaking summer heat

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
articles.description:
While England makes its first foray into unfamiliar territory, it’s proved a boon for Italy’s cash-strapped municipalities 
A nightly tourist tax may be unfamiliar territory in the UK, but countries in continental Europe have been cashing in on these kinds of levies for decades.
Tourists usually need to pay the tax on the day they check out of a hotel or holiday let, and are often surprised by an extra fee on top of their accommodation costs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Much of Europe already levies a tourist tax – a nice little earner for Italian hotspots

It has been a huge week for Labour as Ed Miliband shifted the party’s stance on Israel by announcing sanctions on the illegal settlements in the West Bank and describing what is happening as ethnic cleansing. What is behind this shift, and will it make any difference on the ground?
